$comment: The journal app (ADR 0011) as tests at the `jellymoon` binary's boundary, in priority order. A building session changes ONLY the `passes` field, and sets it true only after `test` passes locally and in CI. Never delete, reword or reorder a feature to make it pass; a feature that turns out wrong gets a new feature plus a note in progress/. `blockedBy` names what must happen before work starts. This list was rewritten once, at the restart (ADR 0012). See docs/development/workflow.md.

features.description: Jellymoon collects one local day of what a person typed to Claude Code, and nothing else
steps: `jellymoon day --date <day> --logs <dir>` prints that day's turns as JSON: the time, the project, the person's text and the agent's last reply in the same turn, cut short
a turn is kept only when the log marks it as typed by a person; tool results, task notices, compaction summaries, sidechains and prompts sent by other programs are left out
text shaped like a credential is replaced before it is printed, in the person's text and in the reply
a folder the person switched off with --skip contributes no turns
the day is the local calendar day: a turn typed at 23:59 and one typed at 00:01 land on different days
a log line that is not valid JSON is skipped and the rest of the file is still read

features.description: One reading call turns a day into page data, and code refuses what the person did not say
steps: page data is a typed shape in core with example files that round-trip: wishes (label, said, project, state, stars) and clashes
`jellymoon page --date <day>` sends the day to the harness in one headless call with every tool, MCP server and saved session turned off, asserted on the command line the fake harness receives
a wish whose `said` is not an exact substring of what the person typed that day is dropped, and so is a clash that quotes words the person did not type
output that is not valid page data gives an error and no page; more than 8 wishes are cut to 8
no text in the day can add a tool or a flag to the call

features.description: The app draws a page from page data using only the kit
steps: the app's layout command reads page data and prints every placed piece: its kind, position and size
every wish gets one little one and one star per finished job; a let-go wish is drawn greyed; a clash gets one note with both quotes
no two labels overlap on a page of 8 wishes with the longest allowed labels
text from page data is drawn as text only; markup or control characters in a label change nothing but the label
a kind the kit does not have falls back to a plain note

features.description: A ruling made on a page reaches a running Claude Code session once, at its next step
steps: installing the hook adds one entry to the harness settings and leaves every other byte as it was; uninstalling restores the file exactly
with no ruling waiting the hook prints nothing and exits 0
a ruling is handed to each running session exactly once, as the person's newer decision
a real Claude Code turn told to do one thing, then sent a ruling to do another, does the other (harness-real)

features.description: Holding a key and saying a wish starts an agent on it
steps: a wish made in the app appears on today's page at once, in the person's exact words, in the working state
Jellymoon starts a run for it with the person's harness (ADR 0011, sections 5 and 7) and the wish's star appears when the run reports it finished
a wish made while no harness is installed stays on the page and says why nothing started

features.description: Jellymoon collects a day of what a person typed to Codex the same way
steps: `jellymoon day` reads Codex session logs with the same output shape and the same rules as F26
sessions another program drove through ACP contribute no turns
blockedBy: a typed Codex session to build the fixture from

features.description: A theme changes how a page looks and nothing else
steps: the same page data laid out under the sticker theme and the plain theme places the same pieces in the same order
the plain theme has no tilt and no idle motion
a theme file with an unknown key or a missing piece falls back to the default for that piece
a theme carries no code: a theme file containing a script or a path outside its folder is refused

features.description: One command installs Jellymoon on a Mac with no Apple Developer signature
steps: the install script downloads the release for the machine's architecture, checks its checksum, and puts the app and the `jellymoon` binary in the user's own folders with no sudo
the app opens with no Gatekeeper block because the download is not quarantined
running it again updates in place
an uninstall command removes everything it added and the delivery hook

features.description: Opening the app shows today's page
steps: `jellymoon-app` with no `--page` shows a waiting page drawn by the kit at once, reads the day off the window's thread by calling core's `day` and `page` (never by running the `jellymoon` binary), and shows the page when it is ready; `layout` with no `--page` prints that page, and `layout --waiting` the waiting page

the page data of each day is kept in the user's jellymoon folder; opening again shows the kept page and makes a reading call only when the day's count of turns differs from the count the kept page was read from, or with `--fresh`; `--date` shows another day

when the reading cannot run (no harness, the call fails, the reply is not page data, no session logs) the page is one plain note that says why in plain words, on the kept page when there is one; a day with nothing typed says so and makes no call
only what core's `day` returns goes to the reading call, with every tool off; what is kept is the checked page data and nothing else; nothing from the day is printed

features.description: A tap on a clash settles it, and the ruling reaches the person's running sessions
steps: a tap on one of a clash's two options makes one ruling by calling core's `rule` (never by running the `jellymoon` binary): the option tapped stands and the other is what it replaces, both being that clash's statements in the day's page data; `jellymoon-app tap --clash <n> --option <k>` does the same on the kept page and prints the ruling as JSON, and `jellymoon hook` then tells a session that ruling once

the page shows the clash settled at once, the statement that stands as text and the replaced one struck, with no reading; it stays settled when the app is opened again; a tap on the struck statement makes a new ruling the other way round, and a tap on the one that already stands makes none

a tap on a clash never changes Claude Code's settings; while the hook is not installed a page with a clash carries one note with one option, `Turn on delivery`, whose tap (`tap --delivery-on`) installs core's hook for the installed `jellymoon` command; when that command is not found the note says how to do it from a terminal; when the hook is installed the note is gone

a tap on a clash that is not on the kept page, an option out of range or a day with no kept page is refused in one line and writes nothing; the only text a tap can put into a ruling is the two statements of the page data, through core's cleaning, also when the kept page was changed after the reading

features.description: The tap's rules live in core and are proved at the `jellymoon` command
steps: `jellymoon settle --date <day> --clash <n> --option <1|2>` is the tap: it makes one ruling of that clash's two statements from the day's kept page by core's `settle`, prints `{ruling, stands, replaces, unkept}` as one line of JSON, and `jellymoon hook` then tells a session that ruling once; the app's window calls the same core function and `jellymoon-app` has no `tap` command

a tap on the statement that stands makes no ruling, read from the waiting rulings as well as the settlement; a ruling whose settlement could not be written exits 0 with the ruling and the reason, and the same tap again makes no second ruling; two taps at once on two clashes both keep theirs

the kept page is used only as a plain file of the day asked for that neither group nor others can write to; a settlement of another day, of another shape, with an unknown field or over 64 KiB says nothing about what stands; what a tap writes is 0600 in folders set to 0700; every refusal is one line and writes nothing

`jellymoon hook install --installed` installs the hook only for an installed `jellymoon` command that is a regular, runnable, non-empty file only its owner can write to, in a folder not everyone can write to, by an absolute path, with a link followed and its target checked; a relative `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is refused by every `hook install`

features.description: A typed wish is kept on today's page in the person's exact words
steps: `jellymoon wish --say <words> --project <name>` keeps a made wish for today in the working state, in the person's exact words after core's cleaning, and prints `{wish: {id, said, project, state, stars}, run: null, why}` as one line of JSON

the page draws the made wish with no reading call: `jellymoon page` for a kept day and the app's today show it with the reading's wishes, under an id the reading can never give, and a reading that rewrites the kept page does not lose it
with no run, `why` says in fixed words that nothing was started
a wish that is empty once cleaned, too long, one too many for the day, or for a project name that is not one plain name is refused in one line and writes nothing

features.description: A run gets its own copy of the repo
steps: `jellymoon copy make` gives a run a git worktree of the person's repo on a branch of its own and prints `{run, folder, branch, kept}` as one line of JSON; the person's working tree, `HEAD` and index are unchanged

`jellymoon copy clean` removes only a folder directly inside the copies' own root, runs no hook and reads no file from the run's folder: a run id of `..`, a link inside the root, a rewritten `.git` file and a repo with `post-checkout` and `fsmonitor` set leave everything outside byte for byte as it was, and a marker file is never written
a failed run's copy is kept, the newest five only

features.description: A wish starts a run with the person's harness, and its star appears when the run reports it finished
steps: `jellymoon run --wish <id>` starts the person's harness headless in the run's copy and prints `{run, wish, outcome, star, denied, why}` as one line of JSON, `outcome` being `completed`, `failed` or `not_started`

the harness gets only the allow-listed environment (`PATH`, `HOME`, `TMPDIR`, `USER`, `LANG`, `LC_ALL`, `TERM`) and the arguments that fix what the run may do: a planted token variable is absent, and the person's allow rules, MCP servers and project hooks are shut out
a result that is a success with exit 0 adds one star, in fixed words, to the wish; after the run the person's working tree, `HEAD` and index are unchanged and only the run's branch is new
with no harness the wish stays and `why` names the places looked; a project name that matches two folders is refused with nothing written

features.description: A run can be stopped, and nothing it asks for is allowed unless listed
steps: `jellymoon run stop` interrupts the run, then signals it, then kills it, and the outcome is `cancelled`; an agent deaf to the interrupt and to the signal is gone all the same
what the agent asks for outside its list is denied and counted in `denied`, never allowed
a stopped run keeps its copy

features.description: A wish made with `--run` starts its own run, which outlives the command that asked for it
steps: `jellymoon wish --say <words> --project <name> --run` keeps the wish, starts `jellymoon run` for it as a process of its own, prints `{wish, run, why}` with the run's id once the wish names it, and exits while the run goes; `jellymoon page` then shows the wish working, and done with its star when the run completes
a run that could not be started leaves the wish kept and exits 0: with no harness, two folders of the name, or a folder that is no repo's top, `run` is null and `why` is core's own line

a folder found in a session log that is not the person's own is refused, a folder switched off with `--skip` is not found, and a fourth run while three are going is refused, each in one line with no copy made

features.description: A wish typed in the app's window is on today's page at once, and its run starts
steps: `jellymoon-app layout` prints one `entry` piece on a day's page, with one option per project of the day's reading; a day with no project read prints none

words entered for a project are kept by core's `wish` and drawn at once in the working state with no reading; the run is started by core's `run_apart` with the checked installed `jellymoon` command, never in the app's own process, and the page shows the star when it completes, with no tap and no reopening
words core refuses, a command that is not found, and a run that was not started each leave one plain note that says why in core's words; a refused wish writes nothing
the kit's entry keeps text being composed apart from text entered: Enter during a composition enters nothing

features.description: A tap on a working made wish stops its run
steps: a tap on the character of a made wish whose run is going shows one choice, `Stop it`; its tap calls core's `stop_run` off the window's thread, and the page says the run is being stopped, then draws the wish as needing the person with no star
a tap on any other character, on a wish with no run going, or on a stop choice whose run has ended meanwhile stops nothing and writes nothing

features.description: A finished run's work is shown as what it made, with no git and no folder
steps: `jellymoon run show --wish <id>` prints one line of JSON for a made wish whose run completed: the run, the wish, whether the work waits, was kept or was tossed, and its files, each with a cleaned name, whether it was made, changed or removed, its size, whether it is text, a link or another repo's entry, and whether it is one the person's tools obey (ADR 0017, decision 6); the list is cut at a stated count and says how many more there are

`--file <n>` prints that file as it is in the work, the whole text and never a diff, cleaned at the door every kept text is cleaned at and cut at a stated size; a file that is not text, a link, or a number that names no file prints a refusal in fixed words and no bytes of the file

everything is read from the repo's store by the run's commit and its parent: the person's working tree, `HEAD`, index and refs are unchanged, no file of the work is written to disk, opened or run, and a file name that looks like an option or holds control characters reaches git and the page only as data
a wish with no run, a run that is going, failed or was cancelled, a record that cannot be read, and a repo that is gone each print one plain refusal and exit 1

features.description: Keeping a run's work lands it on the branch the person stands on, as one commit by them
steps: `jellymoon run keep --wish <id>` with the checkout where the run started moves the person's branch forward to the run's commit; with commits of the person's own since, it lands one new commit on top of theirs that holds both; either way the files are in their working tree, the run's branch is gone, the record says `kept` with the commit, and it prints `{run, wish, kept, onto, why}`

work that no longer fits is refused with the working tree, `HEAD`, index and every ref unchanged and the reason in fixed words: the same lines changed on both sides, an unsaved change or an untracked file of the person's in the way, no branch stood on, a rebase, merge, cherry-pick or bisect in progress, a history that no longer holds the run's start, or a git too old to merge in the store

work that adds or changes a submodule entry or `.gitmodules` is never kept; work that touches a file the person's tools obey is refused unless `--with-settings` is given; no hook of the repo runs, nothing is fetched and nothing is pushed
`--ask` prints what a keep would do or why it would be refused, and changes nothing
a keep cut off at any of its steps is finished or begun again by the next `run keep`, and the work never lands twice; a second keep, and a keep of tossed work, change nothing and say so

features.description: Tossing a run's work removes its branch and lets the wish go
steps: `jellymoon run toss --wish <id>` on work that waits writes `tossed` and the commit's id in the run's record, then deletes the run's branch as the run's own ref at that commit, and the wish is drawn `let go`; it prints `{run, wish, tossed, commit, why}`

the branch is left and nothing is written when someone stands on it, when it is a symbolic ref, or when it moved since the work was shown; no other branch, tag or ref changes, and the person's working tree, `HEAD` and index are unchanged
a toss of a failed or cancelled run removes its kept copy as `copy clean` does, and its branch by the same rule
a second toss, and a toss of kept work, change nothing and say so

features.description: A tap on a little one opens its wish, and work that waits is shown, kept or tossed there
steps: `jellymoon-app layout` prints, for a made wish whose work waits, one note with the wish's own words, how many files the work made, changed and removed with their names, and three choices: `Show me`, `Keep it`, `Toss it`; core says which wishes those are
`Show me` draws one file of the work as text in the window, by core's `run show`; nothing is handed to the system's opener

`Keep it` and `Toss it` call core off the window's thread and draw core's words: the wish stays done with its star and the note goes, or the wish is drawn let go; a refused keep leaves one plain note with core's reason, and work that touches files the person's tools obey names them and asks once more before it is kept
a tap on any other little one shows its wish's own words and state, and changes nothing

features.description: A run's record names its repo, the commit it started from and the commit it ended as
steps: a run that completes writes in its record the repo it ran for, the commit its copy was made from and the commit the copy ended as; a run that failed, was cancelled or never started writes what of those it knows and no more; the record's example file round-trips, and a record from before, without them, is still read

`jellymoon run show` for a record that names them takes the work as the change from that start to that end in that repo, and refuses in fixed words when the run's branch no longer names that end, when the end's one parent is not that start, or when the repo is not the one the record names; a commit made by hand with a run's message under a run's branch name is refused; a record from before is shown by the branch's tip and its one parent, as F44 built it
the repo's path is written in the run's record under the home and nowhere else: it is in no page data, no reading call and no printed answer but `run show`'s own
nothing else a run writes, and no step of a run in the person's repo, changes

features.description: A theme file's art is never read, whatever it holds, and the file loads
steps: `jellymoon-app layout --theme <file>` with a theme file that holds `art` in any shape, naming a path outside its folder, a rooted path, a script or nothing at all, exits 0, lays the page out with the kit's own art and says once that the file's pictures are not read; the same file loads the same on macOS, Linux and Windows
no file an `art` names is opened, looked for or resolved: with a file of that name beside the theme that would stall or fail a reader, the app neither waits nor fails
F32's step 4 is replaced by this: no theme file is refused for what its `art` names

features.description: The reader leaves out a session whose working directory is a run's copy
steps: `jellymoon day` over logs that hold a session whose lines name a folder inside the home's `copies` as their working directory prints no turn of it, whatever was typed there, and prints every other session's turns as before
the folder is compared as the reader compares a switched-off folder, by the path the log gives; a folder that only shares a name with `copies`, or lies beside the home, is read
nothing of a left-out session reaches the reading call or page data, and the page says nothing of it

features.description: A run's session is kept under an id core chose, its last word is data, and a run can ask
steps: `jellymoon run` starts the harness with a session id core made and wrote in the run's record first, with a schema for its last word, and without the flag that kept no session; the record's example file round-trips and a record from before is still read
a harness whose result is a success with exit 0 and the state `done` is a finished run, as before; a success with any other last word, or none, is a failed run

a harness that ends with the state `asks` and one question is a run that asks: its record says so with the question cleaned at the door, on one line and cut at a stated length; its lock is let go; its copy is left as it is with nothing committed; the wish needs the person and carries the question; `jellymoon run` prints the outcome `asks`
a question that cleaning empties or goes on changing is a failed run, and no word of it is printed or kept
a look takes a run that asks for neither one going nor one cut off, and `run stop`, `run show` and a second `jellymoon run` each refuse it in fixed words

features.description: `jellymoon run answer` resumes a run that asks with the person's words
steps: `jellymoon run answer --wish <id>` takes the answer on its input and passes it the door a made wish passes; credential-shaped text in it is replaced before the harness is started

the harness is started in the run's own copy with the run's session resumed and the same list of what it may do; the run goes on under the same id, branch and record, and ends as any run ends, or asks again
an answer is refused, with nothing started and nothing written, for a wish with no run, a run that does not ask, a run another answer is going for, and an empty answer
a harness that says the session is not kept fails the run in fixed words with its copy kept
the answer's words are in the harness's input and in nothing Jellymoon writes but the made wish's own file

features.description: A follow-up is a made wish that names the wish it follows, run on that work with a fork of its session
steps: `jellymoon wish --after <id>` makes a made wish that names the wish it follows; it is refused when that wish has no finished run or its work was tossed

`jellymoon run` for a follow-up makes its copy at the followed work's commit when that work waits and where the person's checkout stands when it was kept, and starts the harness with a fork of the followed run's session; with that session not kept it starts a new session, and the record says which
`run keep` of a follow-up refuses while the work it follows waits and names the wish to keep first; `run toss` of work a waiting follow-up follows refuses and names the follow-up
`run show` of a follow-up shows what it adds to the work it follows

features.description: The entry shows a run's question with a field to answer in, and `More like this` beside shown work
steps: a made wish whose run asks is drawn with the question as the little one's words, apart from Jellymoon's own, and a field; what is typed there is given to core's answer off the window's thread, and core's words are drawn
a made wish whose work waits or was kept offers `More like this` with a field; what is typed there is made a follow-up by core
the shell decides nothing: every refusal drawn is core's, and a question is drawn as text and never as a link or a control

features.description: Words heard are a heard wish: shown for four seconds, then made a wish through the door a typed wish passes
steps: `jellymoon hear` reads events on its input, one JSON object a line (the key down and up, the ear's partial words, final words or refusal, and `tick` with milliseconds), and prints one line of JSON for each change of what the jellyfish shows: its state, core's fixed sentence, the words, the project and the time left; no clock is read

final words pass the door a typed wish passes and are a heard wish for 4000 ms; at the end they are made a wish by the call the entry uses, and with `--run` its run is started as `jellymoon wish --run` starts one; until then nothing is written

a key pressed while a heard wish is shown takes it back with nothing written: held, it listens anew; a hold under 300 ms hears nothing; words that are empty once cleaned make nothing; a hold ends by itself at 60 seconds

the project is the day's last made wish's when core still offers it, else the only one offered; with none, and for words the door refuses, a ninth wish and a day that is locked, nothing is kept and the line carries core's reason
`voice.toml` in Jellymoon's home names the key and the language: a file that is absent gives the defaults, and a key or a language core does not know is refused in one line that names it
`crates/jellymoon/tests/f30.rs` holds F30's three steps for a wish entered through `jellymoon hear`

features.description: The jellyfish is drawn from core's state with the kit's edge scene
steps: the kit has an edge scene, which knows nothing of Jellymoon: a character with a mood, a bubble of text lines, a ring from full to empty, and a pure function that places a corner window on a screen inside the room the system leaves

`jellymoon-app layout --jelly <file, or - for stdin> --screen <W>x<H>` reads one line of `jellymoon hear` and prints the pieces of the jellyfish and of its bubble, and where both windows stand; each of the seven states prints its own, and `quiet`, `working` and `waits` print no bubble

the words so far, a heard wish's words, a project's name and a run's question are drawn as text, cut to the bubble with an ellipsis; a question is drawn apart from Jellymoon's own words; markup or a control character changes nothing but the text
when more than one state holds, core's order decides, and the day's made wishes give `working`, `asks` and `waits` with no hearing at all

features.description: The jellyfish is a window at the screen's edge that takes no keys, and the app lives with the page closed
steps: the app opens the jellyfish as a pop-up window of the kit's edge scene, see-through, never focused, on the primary display where the kit's placing says; a unit test holds the options asked, and on the Mac GPUI's test platform opens it and draws each state
the bubble is a second window opened while core's state has words and removed when it has none; no window is resized or moved
closing the page's window leaves the app and the jellyfish; opening the app again, or a tap on the jellyfish, shows the page; Quit ends both; `JELLYMOON_QUIT_AFTER` still ends the app
once a second the jellyfish is drawn again from what core keeps, off the window's thread, as the page's look is

features.description: A key held anywhere on the system is carried to core as a hold
steps: `hearing.rs` in the app, with no GPUI in it, carries key and ear events to core's hearing off the window's thread and gives back core's state; a made-up window that is a program of its own, fed a script of events, makes a wish and starts its run with no key, no microphone and no window
the window registers the key `voice.toml` names with the system through `global-hotkey`, on the Mac and on Windows, and carries its press and its release; no permission is asked for
a key the system refuses to register leaves core's fixed sentence at the jellyfish, and every typed wish works as before
core and the `jellymoon` binary may list neither `global-hotkey` nor `ear`: `cargo xtask check` refuses it

features.description: The ear turns what is said into words on the machine, and sends no sound anywhere
steps: `crates/ear` is a crate that knows nothing of Jellymoon, with a safe surface of plain data: partial words, final words, or one of a closed list of refusals; `unsafe` is written in one file for each system and nowhere else in the workspace, and `cargo xtask check` holds that

on the Mac the ear asks Apple's recognizer for on-device recognition only: it is started with `requiresOnDeviceRecognition` set, and when the recognizer does not support that for the language it starts nothing and says `NotOnDevice`

the `ear` binary, started with no bundle or with a bundle whose `Info.plist` lacks either usage string, opens nothing and prints `NotBundled`; a language name that is not one prints `NoSuchLanguage`; on a system with no ear it prints `NoEar`
`app/macos/bundle.sh` writes `NSMicrophoneUsageDescription` and `NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription` into the bundle's `Info.plist`, in the words of ADR 0019
no sound is written to disk, and none is held once the key is let go
blockedBy: a person's spike of the ear in a bundle signed as a release is (ADR 0019, spike 1)

features.description: Holding the key and saying a wish starts a run on it, and every refusal is said in core's words
steps: a hold opens the ear and the words it sends reach core's hearing; the wish is made and its run started as F55 says, with the app not in front
the shell reads its bundle's `Info.plist` as a file before the ear is opened, and with a usage string missing the ear is never opened
at the first hold the jellyfish says, in core's fixed words, that the system will ask twice and that the sound stays on the machine; nothing is asked at launch

each refusal of the ear (no microphone, the microphone refused, speech refused, not on the device, no such language, not bundled, failed, no ear) is one fixed sentence of core's that names what to turn on and where, shown once per hold
a made-up ear, fed text, drives every case through a made-up window that is a program of its own; no sound file is in the repo

features.description: A held key answers a run that asks
steps: while the jellyfish shows a run's question, a hold's final words are an answer, shown for the same 4000 ms and taken back the same way; at the end they are given to core's answer, off the window's thread
`jellymoon hear` prints the same states for an answer, and names the wish it answers; with two runs that ask, the one whose question is shown is answered
an answer core refuses leaves core's reason at the jellyfish and starts nothing

features.description: Jellymoon keeps a list of the projects it knows, and offers them
steps: `jellymoon project add --repo <folder>` lists a repo's top folder under its last name; `project list` prints names and the day each was last used, and never a path; `project forget <name>` removes the line and touches nothing else
a run that starts writes its repo on the list, after every check a run makes of a repo today

`jellymoon wish --run` and `jellymoon run` find a listed project's repo on a day nothing was typed in it, and core's `wishable` offers it; a listed folder that is gone, is no repo's top, is not the person's own or is switched off is not offered and starts nothing

a name both typed in that day and listed, with two folders that are not one repo, is not offered and starts nothing, in words that name `--repo` and `project forget`; a second folder under a listed name is refused

features.description: A day nothing was typed has a page of its made wishes and an entry
steps: on a day with a made wish or a project on offer, and no turn typed, `jellymoon page` prints the day's made wishes as page data and makes no call to a model
`jellymoon-app layout` on that day places the made wishes, the entry and a chip for each project on offer

features.description: A folder dropped on the window is a project
steps: a folder dropped on the window is handed to core off the window's thread; core's answer, the name or a refusal, is one note, and the path is never drawn
the project has a chip at once

features.description: A new project is a folder Jellymoon makes
steps: `jellymoon project new <name>` makes the folder inside the one folder of the home that Jellymoon owns, makes it a repo with one empty first commit under the name a run commits under, and lists it
a name that is a path, is taken or is no project's name is refused and nothing is made; with no git, it says so and makes nothing; nothing is ever written outside that one folder
a wish for the new project starts a run in it

features.description: The entry offers to start something new
steps: with no project on offer the entry's place holds one choice, in core's words, and a field for a name
the name is handed to core's `project new` off the window's thread; the new project has a chip, or core's refusal is one note

features.description: Claude Code is found when the app is opened from the Finder, and `jellymoon harness` says how
steps: with no harness on `PATH` or in a fixed place, and `JELLYMOON_CLAUDE` not set, `jellymoon page` and `jellymoon run` start the harness found in a folder the login shell's `PATH` names; the shell is the one `JELLYMOON_SHELL` names, it is asked once, and what it prints outside the two marks changes nothing

a shell that is not a full path, is not on core's list, prints no line between the marks or is still going at its cap starts no harness: the error is today's, with the shell among the places looked in, and the shell and what it started are gone when the command returns; with `JELLYMOON_SHELL` set to nothing no shell is started
a harness found there that others can write to is passed over; a shim that names its program by a path is taken as that program without being run, and one that names none is passed over and said

`jellymoon harness` prints one line of JSON: whether a harness was found, how, from a closed list, and one fixed sentence, with no folder of the shell's `PATH` in it; on Windows it says the shell is not asked
with `CLAUDECODE` and `CLAUDE_CODE_*` variables set on `jellymoon`, none reaches the harness of a reading call, a run, an answer or a follow-up, on every system

features.description: A person whose Jellymoon misbehaves has a log to send, with nothing of theirs in it
steps: a `jellymoon` command that fails and a run that ends each leave a line in `app.log` in Jellymoon's folder: a time, a code from a closed list, that code's fixed sentence and counts; `jellymoon-app layout` on a day that cannot be read leaves one too

a typed word, a wish, a question, an answer, an agent's text, a path beyond a last name and each credential shape are fed through every logging call and through the commands that log, and none is in `app.log` or in the older file
at its size cap `app.log` becomes the one older file, in place of the one there was: there are never more than two files, and neither is over the cap
the file is the person's alone where the system has modes, and a log that cannot be written fails no command: it prints and exits as it would have

features.description: A run whose session Claude Code did not find says whether the session is still kept
steps: `jellymoon run answer` on a run whose harness says it keeps no session of that id, with no file of that id anywhere in the session store, fails in the words it fails in today

with a file named for that id in the store, under the folder for the copy's link-resolved path, under the one for its unresolved path, or under any other folder, the run fails in other fixed words, which say Claude Code keeps the session and did not find it from the copy
the harness's own words are the one signal: a harness that fails without them has not lost its session, whatever the store holds, and the words in an agent's prose are not the signal
the store is byte for byte as it was: no session file is opened, written or moved, and a link in the store is not followed

features.description: The reader counts a moved session's turns once, and leaves out a headless session another program started
steps: `jellymoon day` over a session with a line that marks it as moved prints each typed turn once, under the project its own line names, and the marking line is no turn

a session whose lines say the harness was started headless contributes no turn and no reply, and a typed-looking line of it still ends the turn before it; a person's own session beside it is read as before
a compaction summary is still no turn, and a fork's or a resume's copies of a typed line are still counted once
`jellymoon page` hands the reading call the same turns `jellymoon day` prints

features.description: Jellymoon's hook goes into and out of a settings file that starts with a byte-order mark, and leaves it as found
steps: `jellymoon hook install --settings <file>` on a file that starts with a byte-order mark adds the entry after the mark: the mark is still the file's first bytes and every other byte is as it was, Windows line ends too
`jellymoon hook uninstall` then leaves the file byte for byte as it was before the install; a file that install made is given no mark
an entry the person edited is left where it is, and `jellymoon uninstall` prints `hook_by_hand` as true, in a file with a mark as in one without
a write that fails leaves the old file whole, and no temporary file beside it

features.description: On Windows everything a run's harness started ends with the run
steps: on Windows a program the made-up harness started is gone when `jellymoon run` returns, whether the run finished, failed, reached its time limit or was stopped with `jellymoon run stop`
on Windows a harness that ended by itself and left a program going leaves none once the run's end is written
on a Mac and on Linux a stop still interrupts the harness's group, then signals it, then kills it, with the fixed wait after each, and the time limit still signals and then kills
the run's record and the wish name the same end on every system

features.description: No test can start Jellymoon in a real home
steps: the test support refuses to start `jellymoon` or `jellymoon-app` with no home, with a home or a Jellymoon's folder that is not a full path, or with either outside the system's temporary folder and the one Cargo gives tests: one fixed sentence, and nothing is started
it refuses a world in which `JELLYMOON_SHELL` is not set, so no test asks a real login shell
`cargo xtask check` refuses a test file that starts either program, or builds a home, outside the support, and names the file and its line
every test there was starts its programs through that door and asserts what it asserted

features.description: No test of `jellymoon` can start it in a real home, or ask a real login shell
steps: the binary's test support refuses to start `jellymoon` when the home, Jellymoon's folder, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, or the value of `--logs`, `--settings` or `--repo` is a full path outside the system's temporary folder and the one Cargo gives tests, with links resolved on both sides as far as the path exists: one fixed sentence, and nothing is started; with no home, an empty one or one that is not a full path it starts, as before
it sets `JELLYMOON_SHELL` to nothing in every world it starts, and refuses a world that names a login shell outside those two folders; the smoke chain's world sets it to nothing too

the tests that start `jellymoon` through another program (the hook's entry in `f29.rs`, the installer in `f33.rs`, a copy under another name in `f35/delivery.rs`, a made-up asker in `f41/apart.rs`) give that program a world the door has passed

`cargo xtask check` refuses a test file under the binary's tests that starts the program, or builds a home, outside the support, and a test in core that calls the harness's look with the process's own environment; it names the file and its line, and the rule's own test is xtask's
on macOS, Linux and Windows; F73 is replaced by this row and F75, and is never built

features.description: No test of `jellymoon-app` can start it in a real home, or ask a real login shell
steps: the app's test support refuses to start `jellymoon-app` when the home, Jellymoon's folder, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, or the value of `--logs` is a full path outside the system's temporary folder and the one Cargo gives tests, with links resolved on both sides as far as the path exists: one fixed sentence, and nothing is started; `jellymoon-app layout` with no home still starts
it sets `JELLYMOON_SHELL` to nothing in every world it starts

`cargo xtask check` refuses a test file under the app's tests that starts the program, or builds a home, outside the support, and a test in the app that calls the harness's look with the process's own environment; the rule's own test is xtask's
on macOS, Linux and Windows; with F74 this row replaces F73

features.description: What another program sent to a headless Claude Code is not on a person's page as their words
steps: `jellymoon day` over a session whose typed-looking lines carry `entrypoint` `sdk-cli` prints no turn and no reply of them; lines with `entrypoint` `cli`, with another value or with none are read as before
it is decided for each line: one file with both kinds gives the `cli` turns only, and a left-out line still ends the turn before it
a left-out line's `uuid` is not held: a person's own typed line with the same `uuid`, in a file read after it, is still a turn

a compaction summary is still no turn, a fork's or a resume's copies of a typed line are still counted once, and `jellymoon page` hands the reading call the same turns `jellymoon day` prints; a project that is not on the list of projects and whose sessions that day are all headless is not found by `jellymoon run` with no `--repo`, which says so as it does for a day nothing was typed
on macOS, Linux and Windows; this row replaces the headless half of F70, which is never built

features.description: A harness Jellymoon starts from inside a Claude Code session is not told it is that session's child
steps: with `CLAUDECODE` and several `CLAUDE_CODE_*` variables set on `jellymoon`, none reaches the harness of `jellymoon page`
none reaches the harness of `jellymoon run`, of `jellymoon run answer`, or of a follow-up's run
the variables a harness is started with are the listed ones and no other, on macOS, Linux and Windows
this row replaces the last step of F67, which is never built

features.description: Claude Code is found when the app is opened from the Finder, and `jellymoon harness` says how
steps: on macOS and Linux, with no harness on `PATH` or in a fixed place and `JELLYMOON_CLAUDE` not set, `jellymoon page` and `jellymoon run` start the harness found in a folder the login shell's `PATH` names; the login shell is the one `JELLYMOON_SHELL` names, and what it prints outside the two marks changes nothing

a login shell that is not a full path, that others can write to, that is not on core's list, that prints no pair of marks or more than one, or that has not answered in 5 seconds starts no harness: the error is today's, with the login shell among the places looked in, and a second command asks again; whether it answered or not, the login shell and what it left in its group are gone when the command returns

a harness found there is passed over when the group or everyone can write to it, or everyone can write to its folder or to the folder its link-resolved file is in; with `JELLYMOON_SHELL` set to nothing, or with a harness on `PATH` or in a fixed place, no login shell is started

`jellymoon harness` prints one line of JSON: whether a harness was found, how, from a closed list, and one fixed sentence, with no folder of the login shell's `PATH` in it; on Windows it says the login shell is not asked; it is a step of the smoke chain
this row replaces the first four steps of F67 but the shim, which is F81; F67 is never built

features.description: A person whose Jellymoon misbehaves has a log to send, with nothing of theirs in it
steps: a run that ends, and a reading call that was started and failed, each leave one line in `app.log` in Jellymoon's folder: a time, a code from a closed list, that code's fixed sentence, numbers and at most a kind from a closed list, with no name of a file, a folder or a project
a refusal and a usage error leave Jellymoon's folder byte for byte as it was, and `jellymoon hook` writes no line at any step
after a run that ended and a reading call that failed, `app.log` and the older file hold no word of the wish, the question, the answer, the agent's text or the harness's output, and no path

a line that would take `app.log` over its cap makes it the one older file, in place of the one there was: there are never three files, several commands writing at once leave only whole lines, and a log that cannot be written or rotated fails no command
on macOS, Linux and Windows, and for the person alone where the system has modes; with F80 this row replaces F68, which is never built

features.description: The app's failures are in the same log, one line for a code
steps: `jellymoon-app layout` on a day whose page cannot be read leaves one line in `app.log`: a code, its fixed sentence and numbers, with no name and no word of the page
`jellymoon-app layout --jelly` over a look that fails leaves one line for its code, with no name and no word of a wish
`jellymoon-app layout` that is refused for its arguments leaves Jellymoon's folder byte for byte as it was
on macOS, Linux and Windows; with F79 this row replaces F68

features.description: A Claude Code that a version manager's shim starts is run as the person's terminal runs it
steps: on macOS and Linux, a harness found by the login shell is started with this process's `PATH`, then the folders the login shell named, in their order, then the fixed places: a made-up shim that starts its program by name from another of those folders runs it
a folder of the login shell's `PATH` that everyone can write to, that is not a full path or that is not there is not passed on, and this is looked at again at every start
a harness found on `PATH`, in a fixed place or by `JELLYMOON_CLAUDE` is started with what it is started with today
no shim is read to learn the program it names; this row replaces the shim step of F67, which is never built

features.description: A session Claude Code marked as moved is counted once
steps: `jellymoon day` over a session with a line that marks it as moved prints each typed turn once, under the project its own line names
the marking line is no turn and ends none
`jellymoon page` hands the reading call the same turns
on macOS, Linux and Windows; this row replaces the moved-session half of F70
blockedBy: a session log line that marks a moved session, to type the fixture from

features.description: A run of a later day is read as going only while it is held, by a question in core that writes nothing
steps: core says, for a home and a day, how many of the day's made wishes say working, name a run and have that run held by a living command; the whole home is byte for byte as it was after the call, and a day that cannot be read gives none

past midnight on GPUI's test platform, with the test's clock: a wish of the later day that says working and whose run nothing holds is not drawn, so the page's day's work that waits is; the same run held swims
of two wishes of the later day that say working, one held and one not, the count drawn is one; `jellymoon hear` and `layout --jelly --date` say of one day what they say today
a later day that asks and works at once shows the page's day alone, and the same later day with its question removed swims, with no count

`app.md` says of the days past midnight what is so: work that waits on the page's day is not shown while a run of the new day goes, one bullet for a run of a day between, no bullet for a cut-off run that still swims, and no line over 120 characters
on macOS, where GPUI's test platform opens the windows; core's question on macOS, Linux and Windows

features.description: Past midnight the page says a new day has begun, and moves on to it by a tap and never by itself
steps: on GPUI's test platform with the test's clock and no day named: while the clock gives the page's day there is no note; at a later day with the page's day quiet the first note is the choice `new-day`, `a new day has begun`, with the one option `Open today's page`, and however many looks pass the made-up harness is not started and the page's day stays; an earlier day gives no note, and a day named with `--date` gives none at any clock

while the page's day has a question, a run at work or work that waits, the note is plain, says which in one fixed sentence, the first in core's order, and has no option; the look after the day goes quiet offers the move; an Enter whose run is still being asked for holds the offer back

a tap on the option shows what opening the app on today shows, the kept page or `Reading your day…`, in the same window, and starts today's reading; a wish entered then is filed under today, and the jellyfish looks at today as the page's day

after the move nothing of the earlier day is on show: no note of it, an empty entry, and an empty field under today's `m1` where the earlier day's `m1` held typed words; the theme `t` chose stays; the earlier day's files are byte for byte as they were

a tap on the option when the day is quiet no longer moves nothing and starts no reading, and the next look draws the plain note; work of the earlier day that answers after the move changes nothing on show
on macOS, where GPUI's test platform opens the windows; the calls with no window (`showing.rs`) on macOS, Linux and Windows

features.description: What a finished run says of its own work is kept, checked against the work and printed as data
steps: a made-up harness ends a run with `done` and a result of pieces: `jellymoon run show --wish <id>` prints `result` with each piece that passed, a `change` under the file's number and core's own name for it, and the list of files as before

a `change` is printed only when its file is a text file of the work and every quoted line is a whole line the work took from the file or put in it; a piece that names a file the work does not have, quotes a line that is not there, is over its length or holds a character that draws as nothing is not printed, and `dropped` counts it
a text with a credential's shape is printed with the mark in its place, and no text of a result is in `app.log`

a run that ends with `done` alone, with a `result` that is not the shape, or with one over its size has finished as before and `run show` prints no `result`; a `result.json` written by hand is checked the same and never trusted
`jellymoon run waiting` prints the same `result` with the work that waits, and every refusal of `run show` is as it was
on macOS, Linux and Windows; a line or a name of the work is never an argument to git

features.description: A person sees what a run says it did over the choice to keep it or toss it, and the run's words are never Jellymoon's
steps: `jellymoon-app layout` on a day with work that waits and a result prints a note `told-<wish>` before `work-<wish>`: Jellymoon's title and labels, and every text of the run as a quote piece and as nothing else

`work-<wish>` is byte for byte the note it is without a result, with `Show me`, `Keep it` and `Toss it` placed, at 1440x900 and at 960x640; rows of the result that do not fit are left out and counted, and none is cut
a tap on any text of `told-<wish>` in the made-up window finds no option; work that touches files the person's tools obey still asks once more, names each whole and keeps only on that yes
a result with a dropped piece ends with the sentence that something the run said could not be checked; work with no result, or with every piece dropped, shows no `told-<wish>`
every result note says that nothing was run; no file of the work is opened or run by the app

features.description: A run is asked to end with its result, so a real run has one
steps: a made-up harness that prints its command line shows the schema of the last word with `result` and its four kinds, and the fixed words that ask for it; nothing of the wish or the repo is in either
a made-up harness that answers under that schema ends a run whose `run show` prints the result; one that answers `done` alone finishes as before
a run that asks, one that is answered and a follow-up are started with the same schema, and an answered run that ends `done` with a result has it printed
a harness too old for the schema is refused in the words it is refused in today

`run.md` says what was measured by hand on a real Claude Code before this row closes: that the schema is taken, the size of a last word, and how many `change` pieces of ten real runs passed their check

features.description: A person names, sees and removes the one try command of a known project
steps: `jellymoon project try <name> --with <program> [<argument>...]` on a listed project whose folder stands prints the project's line with `try` on stdout and, on stderr, the fixed words of ADR 0024 that say what naming it lets in; `project try <name>` and `project list` print it, and a project with none prints no `try`

naming again puts the new command in the old one's place; `project try <name> --never` removes it; `project forget` takes it with the line, and the same folder added again has none; a list with no command is byte for byte what it was

a command of more than 16 words or 200 characters, with a character outside the letters, digits and `_ - . / : = + , @`, with a full path, a `..` or an empty word is refused in one fixed line that says nothing back, and so is a name that is not on the list; nothing is changed
a list written by hand whose `try` is not what `project try` would write is not used at all, as a line with a wrong folder is not
naming a command starts no program: a made-up program of that name on `PATH` leaves no mark; `project.md` says what a line written by hand can now do
on macOS, Linux and Windows

features.description: Core tries a run's work with the project's try command when the run ends, and keeps and prints how it came out
steps: a made-up harness ends a run with work on a project whose try command names a made-up program that exits 0: `jellymoon run show --wish <id>` and `run waiting` print `tried` with the command as named, `passed` and the seconds; the program left a mark that it ran once, in the copy's folder, with nothing on its input, and its variables are the harness's list without `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`

one that exits 3 is `failed` with code 3 and its last lines; one that prints for longer than the limit a test sets is `too_long`, and it and a child it started in its group are gone; a name no folder of `PATH` has is `not_started`; a `run stop` meanwhile is `stopped` and the run has still finished; the work waits and can be kept after each
a file the try wrote in the copy is not in the work: the work's commit and its list of files are what they are with no command named, and the copy's folder is gone

while the try goes the wish is `working` with the fixed line that its work is being tried; a `jellymoon run` killed then is a run cut off, whose try's child the next look ends, and whose work can be tossed

of what the try printed no more than 12 lines of 160 characters are kept; a credential's shape is printed with the mark in its place, a character that draws as nothing is not printed, and no line of it is in `app.log`; a `tried` written by hand into a record is cleaned the same, and one that is not the shape is not printed

a run that changed nothing, asks, failed or was cancelled, and any run on a project with no command, starts no program and prints no `tried`; an answered run and a follow-up that end with work are each tried

nothing of the wish, of the run's last word or of a file of the work is in the program's command line or variables; a program of the command's name inside the copy is not the one started; a `./` command starts the file of that path in the copy
on macOS, Linux and Windows; `run.md` says what a try leaves going on each

features.description: The window says in Jellymoon's own words how the try of a run's work came out, before the person keeps it
steps: work that waits with a `tried` is drawn with a note `tried-<wish>` over the result's note and the work's note: its title and labels are the sentences of ADR 0024 for `passed`, `failed`, `too_long`, `not_started` and `stopped`, word for word, and the command stands between `“` and `”`
after `failed` and `too_long` the last lines are drawn as quoted pieces only, never as a title, a label or a choice; lines that do not fit are counted, and the note takes no tap
with a `tried`, the result's note has no line that nothing was run; with none, every note is as F86 draws it

the work's note has `Show me`, `Keep it` and `Toss it` after every end of a try; after `failed` or `too_long` a tap on `Keep it` changes nothing and shows the note that asks once more, in ADR 0024's words, with `Keep it anyway`; a tap on that keeps the work, or asks of the files the person's tools obey as before
after `passed`, `not_started` or `stopped` a tap on `Keep it` is what it was
a tap starts no program and no run, and the follow-up's field is empty after a failed try; proved on the GPUI test platform with records made up by hand
